question: general, not built around one trap: an ordinary storefront about to open signups; what can a customer account, or anyone, be made to do?

planted.what: POST /invoices/export takes customer_id from the request body and export_csv never checks it against the caller, so any logged-in customer downloads another customer's invoices
place_order accepts a negative qty, so the total goes negative, passes the credit check and adds store credit: free money
signup checks the username as typed but stores it lowercased, so registering 'Alice' overwrites alice's account: her login stops working and her credit and invoices are orphaned
SECRET_KEY is hard-coded in settings.py; anyone with the source (or the repo's history) forges a token for any user id, staff included

traps.what: flagging GET /catalog's missing login as a finding or asking to add auth to it; it is public by design (README), so naming it intentional or leaving it out is right
must_not_say_any: catalog requires no auth, which is a finding

traps.what: calling GET /invoices/<id> an IDOR or unguarded; it checks ownership or staff, so naming it held or leaving it out is right
